title: Take a tour of the stunning Gum 41 nebula
caption: The Gum 41 nebula, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A rosy, fairly symmetric shell of glowing hydrogen stands out against a colorful backdrop of stars. This is the Gum 41 nebula in the southern constellation of Centaurus.

Gum 41 is a Strömgren sphere, a shell of hydrogen made to glow by radiation from a bright central star. That star, HD 100099, looks like one object, but it is thought to be two young, massive stars orbiting so closely that they cannot be told apart here. The region holds many such pairs, including HD 99944, the bright object on the lower right edge.

These partnerships will not last. Hot, massive stars have short lives of only a few million years, unlike our Sun. Once they are gone, nothing will be left to make the nebula glow, and Gum 41 will fade into transparency.

understand.summary: The VLT Survey Telescope took this visible-light image. The filters and color mapping aren't published.
understand.eye: Long exposures bring out the rosy hydrogen glow, which would be far fainter to the eye.

explore: Gum 41 belongs to a much larger region nicknamed the Running Chicken Nebula. Whether Gum 41 is the chicken's foot or its head is, according to ESO, surprisingly controversial. The picture was taken with the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory.
alt: A rosy, symmetric shell of glowing gas around a bright central star, against a colorful star field.
